title: Microsoft 365 admin center: migrate Google Groups to Microsoft 365 Groups
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned conversation-migration service from the documented Google Identity Sync tool. The roadmap facts and existing group controls are supported; the membership path could be completed with the final owner or member choice and action.

claims.claim: The planned service is in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The planned service migrates Google Groups into Microsoft 365 Groups for customers moving from Google.
claims.quote: Google compete customers moving to M365 would have the ability to automatically create the groups

claims.claim: The planned service creates the groups' members in Microsoft 365 Groups.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync provides one-way synchronisation of user and group identities from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Google Identity Sync provides one-way synchronization of user and group identities from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Google Identity Sync maps source Google Workspace groups to Microsoft 365 unified groups.
claims.quote: Each source Google Workspace group is mapped to a Microsoft 365 unified group, using the default Microsoft 365 domain for the group email address.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync synchronises group owners and members.
claims.quote: If a destination owner or member doesn't exist in the Microsoft 365 group, the user is added with the appropriate role (Owner or Member).

claims.claim: The Google Identity Sync page documents identity synchronisation rather than conversation migration.
claims.quote: Searched: Google Groups migration conversations permissions admin center; opened and read the full Google Identity Sync page, including group mapping, members sync and re-sync. It describes identities and assignments, not migration of conversation content.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync maps Google Owner to Microsoft 365 Owner.
claims.quote: Google Workspace group members with the Owner or Manager role are mapped to the Owner role in the corresponding Microsoft 365 group.

claims.quote: Google Workspace group members with the Owner or Manager role are mapped to the Owner role in the corresponding Microsoft 365 group.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync maps Google Member to Microsoft 365 Member.
claims.quote: Google Workspace group members with the Member role are mapped to the Member role in the Microsoft 365 group.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync does not synchronise external users.
claims.quote: External users and custom-permission members are not synchronized.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync does not synchronise custom-permission members.
claims.quote: External users and custom-permission members are not synchronized.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync re-sync can remove member and owner assignments added only in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Re-sync can remove member and owner assignments added only in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Google Identity Sync users need licences for the Microsoft 365 services being migrated to.
claims.quote: Once user synchronization is complete and verified, assign users the licenses required for the Microsoft 365 services you're migrating to.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 group membership grants access to the group's content and resources.
claims.quote: Members - Access all group resources but can't change group settings.

claims.claim: The user group-creation setting is at Microsoft Entra ID > All groups > Groups > General settings > Users can create Microsoft 365 groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell.
claims.quote: Select Microsoft Entra ID. Select All groups > Groups, and then select General settings. ... Set Users can create Microsoft 365 groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell to Yes or No.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/groupSettings/{groupSettingId} updates a tenant-wide group setting.

claims.claim: The group-creation control uses EnableGroupCreation within the group setting's values.
claims.quote: To configure the Users can create Microsoft 365 groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell setting by using Microsoft Graph, configure the EnableGroupCreation object in the groupSettings object.

claims.claim: The group-creation settings apply to users.

claims.claim: Teams & groups > Active teams & groups > group > Membership reaches group owner and member management in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Expand Teams & groups ... Active teams & groups. ... Click the name of the group ... On the Membership tab, choose ... Owners or Members. ... Choose Add ... or click X
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Teams & groups > Active teams & groups > group > Membership > Owners or Members > Add or X', retaining the note that Add adds someone and X removes someone, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/create-groups/manage-groups.

claims.claim: On Membership, choose Owners or Members to select which assignments to manage.
claims.quote: On the Membership tab, choose if you want to manage Owners or Members.

claims.claim: Add adds someone to the selected group assignment.
claims.quote: Choose Add to add someone or click X to remove someone.

claims.claim: X removes someone from the selected group assignment.
claims.quote: Choose Add to add someone or click X to remove someone.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/groups/{group-id}/members/$ref adds members, rather than owners, to a Microsoft 365 group.
claims.quote: Add a member to a security or Microsoft 365 group. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/{group-id}/members/$ref

claims.claim: The POST request body sets @odata.id to a reference to the user being added.
claims.quote: When using the POST /groups/{group-id}/members/$ref syntax, supply a JSON object that contains an @odata.id property with a reference by ID to a supported group member object type.

claims.claim: In delegated scenarios, the signed-in user adding members needs a supported role such as Groups Administrator or must be a group owner.
